evidence: src/application/CatalogueService.ts addProduct: builds a Product object and calls catalogue.addProduct, which is use-case orchestration.

src/application/CatalogueService.ts getProductWithStock: returns null when the product is missing and otherwise combines domain query results into a DTO. The stock figures come from Catalogue methods.
src/application/CatalogueService.ts getAllProductsWithStock: maps the domain products into a read model and does no calculation itself.
No database, HTTP, filesystem or framework code anywhere in the file.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: CatalogueService is a plain application service that coordinates use cases. addProduct builds a Product value and hands it to the domain Catalogue. getProductWithStock and getAllProductsWithStock put together read models by calling Catalogue query methods (getAvailableStock, getReservedStock, getTotalStock). The file contains no persistence, transport, HTTP or framework code. The only logic is a null check and mapping results into DTO shapes, so it carries no business rules or invariants such as stock calculations or reservation logic. Those stay in the domain Catalogue. Every responsibility fits the application layer.
